name: Quantitative analysis
description: Measured quantities: define the metric, keep the denominator honest, prefer the distribution to the average, report uncertainty.
body:
# Quantitative analysis domain profile

What the subject itself demands when the artifact is a measurement, a model or a claim about numbers. Role and base conduct are unchanged; this adds only the methods the material requires.

## What the subject asks for

- **Define the quantity before measuring it.** State the metric, its unit, its denominator and the population it covers. A ratio whose denominator is unstated is not yet a result.
- **Keep the sample honest.** Name what entered the sample and what did not. A population filtered by an earlier outcome — only the survivors, only the accepted, only the fast — measures the filter, not the work.
- **Prefer the distribution to the average.** Report the spread, the quantiles and the sample size beside any point estimate. Tails and rare worst cases usually decide the decision, and a mean hides both.
- **Separate measurement from interpretation.** Label each number as measured (with the query, command or file it came from), derived (with the formula) or assumed. Do not launder an assumption through a calculation.
- **Give uncertainty in the units of the decision.** State the interval or range that would change the conclusion, and the observation that would narrow it. A confidence figure must come from a model or a measurement; otherwise say the uncertainty is qualitative.
- **Make it reproducible.** Keep the script, the input snapshot and the exact filter so another person can re-run the numbers and get the same result.
- **Beware arithmetic comfort.** A tidy model, a weighting scheme or a composite score can manufacture a winner. Prefer the simplest comparison that answers the question, and say plainly when no comparison is possible.

## Deliverable

The result, the numbers it rests on with their provenance, the uncertainty that bounds it, and what would falsify it.

This profile guides behavior. It does not enforce gates, prove truth, install hooks, or grant any permission.
